title: Hypothesis-driven eval capture and postmortem automation for incident-driven regressions
creator: Priya Raman
description:
Background: A recent production incident (2026-02-15) surfaced a quality regression after a config change to prefix-KV TTL + batching throttle. The incident revealed gaps in our post-incident eval artifacts: we could reproduce failures manually but lacked an automated way to capture the minimal failing input/config footprint, generate targeted evals, and persist those as smoke tests tied to the rollout.

Goal: Build a small, hypothesis-driven capture + test generation flow that automatically produces a compact, high-signal eval set and a postmortem artifact when an incident is opened for config/model regressions. Deliverables should include: 1) an automated capture runner that replays sampled requests against pre/post config snapshots and emits minimal failing inputs, 2) a generator that expands minimal cases into a targetted synthetic eval set (mutations, prompt variants, seq-length sweeps), 3) an automated PR template and smoke-test artifact that can be checked into the runtime/eval repos, and 4) an integration point for the postmortem doc and incident timeline.

Approach / Implementation plan:
- When an incident is triaged as a config/model regression, the capture runner will: snapshot the config diff, pull a bounded sample of recent requests (respecting PII filters), and run those requests against both snapshots in an isolated harness.
- The system will compute per-example diffs (outputs + token-level scoring) and rank candidates by regression magnitude and coverage of edge axes (prefix length, quantization path, tokenization boundary).
- From top candidates, generate 30–200 synthetic variants (prompt paraphrases, shorter/longer prefixes, repeat-token stress) to find minimal failing patterns.
- Persist the curated set as a JSONL artifact with metadata (config diff, commit ids, experiment seed) and auto-open a draft PR in the eval-smoke-tests repo with a test harness wrapper.
- Surface the artifact link in the incident postmortem and Console bugcard (dashboard snapshot link + thresholds).

Success metrics:
- Mean time from incident triage to usable failing-eval artifact <= 24h.
- Fraction of incident regressions with an automated smoke test created >= 70% in Q2.
- False-positive rate of generated smoke tests <= 10% (manual triage).

Trade-offs / Notes:
- Requires access to request logs for the relevant window; private deployments may have shorter retention—ops involvement required.
- Synthetic mutations reduce reliance on large labeled datasets but can overfit to a modeled hypothesis; keep human-in-the-loop approval before committing tests.
- Must ensure artifacts are scrubbed for customer data and comply with retention/KMS rules.

Deliverables / Acceptance:
- capture-runner service + CLI (containerized) that accepts incident id and outputs artifact URL.
- test-generator library (python) that produces JSONL and a ready-to-merge PR.
- incident postmortem template linked automatically to the artifact.
- documentation + runbook for on-call to trigger manual runs.

Open questions / blockers:
- Do we have sufficient historical request retention for private customers? (Ops action required)
- Should generated tests live in runtime repo or a dedicated ops-evals repo? (security + release implications)
- How to gate auto-PRs for sensitive customers? (opt-out/whitelist)

Longer-term: Replace this with a live canary that detects config-induced quality regressions pre-rollout by comparing control vs candidate snapshots on sampled realtime traffic (subject to privacy/throughput constraints).
comments: 2026-02-20 — Triage note: Incident 2026-02-15 assigned; initial hypothesis is interaction between prefix-KV TTL and late-token quantization path. Priya opened this ticket to capture follow-ups from the postmortem.
2026-02-22 — Miguel: PoC capture runner done (local): replays 200 samples, computes delta-score using existing eval metrics. PoC located at https://github.com/redwood-inference/capture-poa (WIP).

2026-02-24 — Aisha Nguyen (Review): Suggested adding tokenization-boundary checks and ranking by top-k disagreement as well as log-prob delta. Also flagged privacy scrub requirement (see Confluence link).
2026-03-01 — QA run: synthetic generator produced 1,200 variants from 12 seed failures; manual triage reduced to 48 high-confidence failing cases (4% false positive).
2026-03-04 — Blocking: Ops needs to enable 90-day request retention for private vpc-ops customers to allow capture; raised ENG-62102 to track that toggle.

2026-03-07 — PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-smoke-tests/pull/402 — draft PR contains harness + auto-generated tests for runtime-blocking-2026-02. Miguel requesting review from Aisha and Jordan.

2026-03-10 — Decision: Auto-PRs will be draft by default; require human approval before merge. Added opt-out flag for customer-sensitive artifacts. Next: wire webhook from incidents service to trigger capture-runner (owner: infra).
